questions.title: Minimum Path Sum in the Grid
questions.description:
A delivery drone crosses an R x C cost grid from the top-left to the bottom-right cell, moving only right or down; every entered cell adds its cost (the start cell counts too). Return the minimum total cost of any such path — fill the cost table in place (sort( is banned). Input format: line 1 has R and C; each of the next R lines has C integers. The harness builds grid (vector<vector<long long>>). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long min_path_sum(const std::vector<std::vector<long long>>& grid)

Input Format:
Line 1: R and C. Next R lines: C integers each.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum path cost.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 15, 1 <= grid[r][c] <= 1000

questions.title: Fibonacci Term
questions.description:
The Fibonacci sequence starts f(0) = 0, f(1) = 1 and every later term is the sum of the two before it. Return f(n) for a given n — fill the table bottom-up instead of recomputing branches recursively. Input format: a single line with n. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long fib_term(long long n)

Input Format:
Line 1: n.

Output Format:
One line with f(n).

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Unique Paths in the Grid
questions.description:
A warehouse robot starts at the top-left cell of an R x C floor and walks to the bottom-right cell, moving only right or down one cell at a time. Return the number of distinct paths — fill the paths table dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1] (factorial( binomials are banned). Input format: line 1 has R and C. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long grid_paths(long long R, long long C)

Input Format:
Line 1: R and C.

Output Format:
One line with the number of paths.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 15

questions.title: Climbing Stairs Ways
questions.description:
You climb a staircase of n steps, taking either 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct orderings of moves that reach the top — the classic recurrence ways(n) = ways(n-1) + ways(n-2), seeded ways(1) = 1 and ways(2) = 2. Input format: a single line with n. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long stair_ways(long long n)

Input Format:
Line 1: n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of ways.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 40

questions.title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
questions.description:
A staircase charges cost[i] the moment you step on stair i. You may start on stair 0 or stair 1, and from a stair you climb 1 or 2 stairs at a time. Return the minimum total cost to get PAST the top (index n) — you never pay for a stair you never step on. Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n integers. The harness collects them in a vector<long long>, in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long min_climb_cost(const std::vector<long long>& cost)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n stair costs.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum cost to reach past the top.

Constraints:
2 <= n <= 40, 1 <= cost[i] <= 1000

questions.title: 0/1 Knapsack Max Value
questions.description:
A courier packs a knapsack of capacity W: item i weighs wt[i] and is worth val[i], and each item may be taken at most once. Return the maximum total value that fits without exceeding the capacity — the classic 0/1 knapsack table over (items seen, remaining capacity). Input format: line 1 has n and W; line 2 has n weights; line 3 has n values. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long knapsack_value(const std::vector<long long>& wt, const std::vector<long long>& val, long long W)

Input Format:
Line 1: n and W. Line 2: n weights. Line 3: n values.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum value.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= W <= 500, 1 <= wt[i] <= 100, 1 <= val[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Longest Common Subsequence Length
questions.description:
Two version strings share characters that appear in both, in the same order (not necessarily adjacent). Return the length of their longest common subsequence — the classic 2-D table over prefixes of a and b. Input format: line 1 has string a; line 2 has string b (lowercase letters, no spaces). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long lcs_length(const std::string& a, const std::string& b)

Input Format:
Line 1: string a. Line 2: string b.

Output Format:
One line with the LCS length.

Constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 50, both strings use lowercase letters

questions.title: Frog Jump Minimum Energy
questions.description:
A frog crosses stones numbered 0..n-1, starting on stone 0 and heading for stone n-1. From stone i it can jump to i+1 or i+2, and a jump spends energy equal to the absolute height difference |h[i] - h[goal]|. Return the minimum total energy for the crossing (0 when there is a single stone). Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n integers. The harness collects them in a vector<long long>, in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long frog_min_energy(const std::vector<long long>& h)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n stone heights.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum total energy.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 50, 1 <= h[i] <= 1000

questions.title: Coin Combination Count
questions.description:
A vending machine stocks coins of a few denominations and reports how many combinations make an amount: return the number of unordered ways to form amount using UNLIMITED coins of each denomination (2+1 and 1+2 count once). Fill the ways table coin by coin. Input format: line 1 has k (number of denominations); line 2 has k distinct denominations; line 3 has the amount. The harness collects the denominations in a vector<long long> coins. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long coin_ways(const std::vector<long long>& coins, long long amount)

Input Format:
Line 1: k. Line 2: k denominations. Line 3: amount.

Output Format:
One line with the number of unordered combinations.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 8, 1 <= coins[i] <= 100, 1 <= amount <= 200

questions.description:

Input Format:
Line 1: string a. Line 2: string b.

Output Format:
One line with the longest common substring length.

1 <= |a|, |b| <= 30, both strings use lowercase letters

questions.title: Loyalty Points Ladder
questions.description:
A loyalty scheme seeds day 1 with a points and day 2 with b points; from day 3 on, the day's award equals the sum of the previous two days' awards. Return the award granted on day n. Input format: line 1 has n, a and b. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Line 1: n, a and b.

Output Format:
One line with the day-n award.

1 <= n <= 40, 1 <= a, b <= 1000

questions.title: Pavement Tiling Ways
questions.description:
A courtyard path is a 2 x n grid to be paved with 2 x 1 tiles placed vertically or horizontally. Return the number of distinct tilings — the Fibonacci-style recurrence t(n) = t(n-1) + t(n-2), seeded t(1) = 1 and t(2) = 2. Input format: a single line with n. Input Format:
Line 1: n.

Output Format:

questions.title: Minimum Coins for Change
questions.description:
A till must make an exact change with the fewest coins, but the denominations are arbitrary (unlimited supply of each): return the minimum number of coins summing to amount, or -1 when it cannot be made. Greedy picking fails on arbitrary denominations — build the full DP table (sort( is banned; nothing gets reordered). Input format: line 1 has k (number of denominations); line 2 has k distinct denominations; line 3 has the amount. The harness collects the denominations in a vector<long long> coins. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long min_coins(const std::vector<long long>& coins, long long amount)

Input Format:
Line 1: k. Line 2: k denominations. Line 3: amount.

Output Format:
One line with the minimum number of coins, or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= k <= 10, 1 <= coins[i] <= 500, 1 <= amount <= 5000

A burglar cases a street of houses: looting two ADJACENT houses triggers the alarm. Return the maximum total loot over any set of houses with no two adjacent — fill the loot table where dp[i] is the best over the first i+1 houses (sort( is banned). Output Format:
One line with the maximum loot.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= val[i] <= 10000

questions.title: Partition Into Equal Sums
questions.description:
A storage audit asks whether a shipment can be split into two parcels of exactly equal total weight: return 1 when some subset of the items sums to half the total, else 0 (an odd total can never split). Fill the subset-reachability table over sums up to total/2 (sort( is banned). Input format: line 1 has n; line 2 has n integers. The harness collects them in a vector<long long>, in input order. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int can_partition(const std::vector<long long>& val)

Input Format:
Line 1: n. Line 2: n item weights.

Output Format:
One line: 1 if an equal split exists, else 0.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 20, 1 <= val[i] <= 200

One line with the longest palindromic subsequence length.

1 <= |s| <= 30, s uses lowercase letters

questions.description:
A timber yard cuts a rod of length L into whole-length pieces; a piece of length i sells for price[i] (i = 1..L). Return the maximum total revenue achievable — leaving the rod uncut is allowed. Fill the revenue table dp[len] over every prefix length (sort( is banned). Input format: line 1 has L; line 2 has L prices, price[i] for piece length i. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    long long rod_revenue(long long L, const std::vector<long long>& price)

Input Format:
Line 1: L. Line 2: L prices.

Output Format:
One line with the maximum revenue.

Constraints:
1 <= L <= 40, 1 <= price[i] <= 1000

    int lis_length(const std::vector<long long>& a)

Line 1: n. Line 2: n values.

One line with the LIS length.

1 <= n <= 200, 1 <= a[i] <= 100000

    long long count_subsets(const std::vector<long long>& val, long long target)
